utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you mentioned earlier on that -- I think it was on 1st November 1991, you entered into a form of co-operation with the JNA. Is that correct? I didn't hear your answer, sorry. I did not hear --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Correct, correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Very well. What was that co-operation? Can you describe it for us? How did it come about, and what did it imply?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: On the 1st of October, 1991, the state of an imminent threat of war was proclaimed in the territory of Yugoslavia. The JNA launched an active fight against the secessionist forces. There was no longer need for us to send volunteers through Territorial Defence staffs. We could do it directly through the JNA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understand. Why did the proclamation of a state of imminent threat of war imply that you did not any longer have to send volunteers through the TOs? I mean, I suppose that the TOs were still requesting assistance. Weren't they?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: The thing is that from the time the imminent state of war was proclaimed, the JNA got involved in armed clashes with secessionist forces. Until then, it had been neutral.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Right. But even after the JNA engaged itself in armed conflicts with the separationist forces, I suppose that the TOs and the local crisis staffs out there in Croatia would still request assistance from the SRS. Wouldn't they?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. But I just explained a moment ago the Territorial Defence is an integral part of the JNA, so it's under the direct command of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: After 1st October 1991, who sent requests to the SRS for assistance?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Territorial Defence staffs, but under the direct command of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But how was the procedure different?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: The procedure was different because we were able to address ourselves directly to the JNA to get weapons, uniforms, transportation, and everything else that was needed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Right. So basically you were still dealing with the TOs, and the difference was just that now the TOs were under the command of the JNA; is that how it's to be understood?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Roughly, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So in your view, after October 1st it was now the JNA that issued requests to the SRS asking for volunteers to arrive and to assist in the armed conflicts; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Indirectly, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And directly?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Directly, it was the Staff of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Did you also, from time to time, provide volunteers to the MUP?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: We never sent volunteers to the MUP. All the volunteers we had were engaged by the local MUPs in Croatia. We have to get one thing clear. It was not the MUP of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And do you know if, in 1992, albeit after you had resigned, that the SRS provided volunteers not only to the JNA, or would then eventually become the VRS, but also to the MUP, the Serbian MUP in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: I heard that some volunteers were engaged in the Serbian MUP of Bosnia and Herzegovina, but I'm really not qualified to speak about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: After you had resigned, when we move into 1992, and again I know that you had resigned so you may not have first-hand knowledge of this, but do you happen to know how the organisation was -- or how the provision of volunteers to the VRS was organised? Did that follow the same routine as with the JNA earlier on; namely, that it would be the local TOs or the crisis staffs in Bosnia and Herzegovina who would ask for assistance from the SRS for volunteers? In other words, did the procedure continue roughly along the same lines into 1992; do you know?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Do you know if the SRS ever provided any uniforms or weapons to the volunteers?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: The SRS never had any weapons or uniforms. Only the JNA could provide that; and the MUP of Serbia, which had weapons and uniforms, but we did not have any co-operation with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So to your knowledge, the volunteers were never dispatched to the police, to the MUP, and therefore never went into the MUP organisation and under the MUP command? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: While I was deputy chief of the War Staff, I can say with full responsibility that not a single volunteer went anywhere through the MUP of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: You mentioned, though, that in some instances volunteers moved on from having fought under the command of the TO, and after the battle they moved on and signed up with the MUP, so my question is: Did you still retain contacts with those volunteers who left the TO and started working with the MUP, or did you lose contact with them as of that point?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: From that moment on, they were no longer our responsibility. They were the responsibility of the local MUP. They were on the payroll of that MUP, and they belonged to a different agency, a different structure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So your organisation of volunteers was limited to providing volunteers to, first, the TOs, and then after October 1st, 1991, to the JNA, and that is as far as the co-operation between the SRS and the armed forces went; is that correctly understood? For the record, sir, please provide your answer. I saw that you were nodding, but you have to say something.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thanks. My final question relates to a piece of information that I also read somewhere in the statements about information that you did receive of insubordination on the part of some of the volunteers that you had sent. I think you mentioned -- you used the word, somewhere in your statements, the word "independently," that small units of former volunteers started to act independently. What exactly did you mean by that word? Do you remember having said that, and do you understand the meaning of my question? What happened with these guys? What did they do?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me -- could you give me a reference? What cases are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I think there was an incident in the municipality of Zvornik, where some SRS volunteers had been registered with the TO, but subsequently started to act, and this was your word, independently. And I was curious to know what actually you meant by that --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: I would appreciate it if you made a distinction between 1991 and 1992. Zvornik was 1992. 1992 can only be what I know from hearsay and may not be true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Very well. My last question to you, Mr. Rankic, is -- and let me go back a bit to the point where you were handing over your volunteers to the TO command. Do you know if the volunteers were told that they could stay together as a unit, while they were under the TO command, once the fighting started?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Well, for the most part, they acted as units together, because they knew each other best, they knew their commander best, so it was logical for them to act as a unit, but, of course, within the Territorial Defence and with specified tasks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But maybe this is where the word "independently" comes in. Do you know if they were allowed to act independently, of course, still under the overall command of the TO? But while in combat, did they have their own leader with them and able to carry out the orders independently?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: In the field, every unit would get a certain task, an assignment. However, the executive command in the field belongs to the Command of the TO. That means that all units act in a synchronised way as part of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are now going to move to questions put to you by Judge Lattanzi, and I'm not going to interrupt her.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Witness, good afternoon. I need to get some clarification on some preliminary issues regarding all those parties. It seems that as in Italy, you have tens and tens of parties, and I'm rather confused. We are talking about the Serbian Radical Party. Could you perhaps give me the acronym in your own language?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: SRS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Then you have the Popular -- or People's Radical Party. Could you perhaps give me the acronym in your language? Perhaps it's not the correct translation, but this is the party of which you were a member, if I'm not mistaken. What was the acronym in your own language?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: You just inverted the word order. It's the Popular Radical Party, NRS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] NRS. Very well. And then we hear of the SNO, and I don't quite understand what this is about. Do you know anything about that ?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: It's the Serbian People's Renewal, led by Mirko Jovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ah, okay, very well. Thank you. And then we have the MCS, which is the Serbian Chetnik Movement; right? MC, with the sign on top, and this is the movement -- the Serbian Chetnik Movement. But what is the acronym in your own language, please?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: The acronym for the Serbian Chetnik Movement is SC, with a diacritic, P.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Now I can find my way through this, because I was rather confused. You talked at length with Judge Harhoff on the recruitment within the party, and namely the Serbian Radical Party, and you were very well informed, even if you were not a member of the Serbian Radical Party, because you told us this afternoon that you did not take part in the setting up of the Serbian Radical Party and you never had a membership card. So you were very well informed, as you told us, but I would like us to confirm or deny that. As I was saying, you were very well informed, because you said to us this afternoon that you worked at the headquarter, and even if, like Mr. Seselj, you were part of this wider movement, namely, the Serbian Chetnik Movement, you said that, We were working like a unit. You said this this afternoon; correct? I can give you the reference in the transcript. It's page 38, from lines 5 to 7. So what I would like to know is to have more information, basically, on the volunteers of this wider movement, as well as volunteers from the Serbian Radical Party. What was their relationship? Were they all organised in the form of a single unit, even when it comes to the various branches of the Serbian Radical Party, be it in Belgrade or elsewhere, whether buses that were organised were boarded by all of them? Was there really a single unit that you mentioned? And if that is true, as you have testified this afternoon, if it is true that we were talking about all those volunteers as the Chetnik volunteers?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: I can tell you about the enemy force. They called us all Chetniks, whereas we, amongst us, knew who was who.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But the volunteers that were specifically organised by the Serbian Radical Party, under the authority -- the political authority and the moral authority of the accused, were they also considered as Chetnik volunteers; is that how we referred to them, Chetnici [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, we were all called Chetniks, and they called even the JNA Chetniks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now I would like to touch upon another issue. At some stage in your testimony, you said that all those Chetnik volunteers had the possibility to organise themselves and then to work towards defending the Serbian people, as you said. Now, before mobilisation, before there was a danger that was announced, there was a law, if you will, that stated that after this point in time, something happened, and then you had a unit, you had the TO, you had the army, you had the volunteers, and so on and so forth. But what I would like to know, I would like to know when volunteers were organised. Was that before the mobilisation in 1991, and was it before it was declared that there was an imminent threat of war? I would like to know when volunteers started to be recruited, because there were perhaps one-off volunteers that signed up after the mobilisation and after Yugoslavia decided to mobilise its troops, because you also mentioned volunteers -- one-off volunteers or individual volunteers who signed up, but that was after mobilisation. Okay. And from what I understood in your testimony today, you already had volunteers that had organised themselves through the various political parties, through this Chetnik movement, and so what I would like to know is when this started.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Beginning with 2nd May, the attack at Borovo village by units of the Croatian MUP. From that moment on, we started sending volunteers across the Danube.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay, after Borovo Selo. Yes, thank you. What I wanted to know is the following: They could not get the help from the TO or from the JNA, or could they already get help from the TO already at that stage? When it comes to equipment, to weapons, and to logistics, did they immediately get help from the TO?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: From the TO, yes. From the JNA, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So they received weapons from the TO. The TO had weapons at their disposal, or was it that the TO received weapons only after national mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: The Territorial Defence already had weapons at their disposal, but those were mostly old, perhaps obsolete weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So it means that the TO had weapons even during peacetime. Even if these were obsolete or unsophisticated weapons, they could keep those weapons during peacetime?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that was the rule in the former SFRY.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. In your testimony, you also talked about SAVA. I think that you mentioned that when Judge Harhoff put some questions to you, or perhaps Judge Antonetti. You talked about the Association of Serbs abroad. Was that called "SAVA"?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: No, those are two different organisations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apology. At some stage, the association, SAVA, disappeared, and this new Party of Serbian Renewal came about; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Correct. Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And this new Party of Serbian Renewal, did it have a similar ideology to defend the Serbian people?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: For the most part, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Talking about this ideology, I was wondering whether you could be more precise. What did this mean, and defending the Serbian people? Did this involve defending, stricto sensu, oneself against somebody else who's attacking you, or was it also in the aim of gaining some territory? We're talking about this border and the concept of a Greater Serbia, because it's important. You said that volunteers started to organise themselves around defending the Serbian people, so I would like to know exactly what was meant by that.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: The idea to defend the Serbian people depends on the year. If we're talking about in the year 1990, when the Serbian National Defence was established, then we meant to defend the Serbian traditions, the culture, script. And if you're talking about the period when the armed conflict started, it was about defending Serbs who resided outside of the territory of the then Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And this Serbian defence outside the territory of Serbia - I'm not talking about Yugoslavia, I'm talking about Serbia - I was wondering whether it meant extending the territory of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: In the areas that we went to, Serbs were a majority population, for the most part. I don't know what you mean when you say "extending the territory of Serbia."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to come back to this point. You were saying that Serbs were a majority population, which means, according to you, that this territory should be part of Greater Serbia?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: I don't use that term at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So what word would you use?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: We were against the fragmentation of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You were against the fragmentation of Yugoslavia. Indeed, I understand that very well, and I also understand how this attempt came about to be against any secession. But once you understood that secession was unavoidable, and when you realised -- or when you saw that the ideology of a Greater Serbia developed, in a way it meant that Serbia would become Greater Serbia, including occupied territories when there was -- where Serbs were a majority population in Bosnia, specifically?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I don't know what you mean when you say "the Greater Serbia." Serbia did not start existing in 1945, but in 1918.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's leave that aside. Greater Serbia was a political ideal, I believe. But if you are not aware of this, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I have to provide a very brief explanation, if the Trial Chamber allows me to do so. This is what it is about: In 1918, Serbia proclaimed its western borders on the Kupa and Ilok [as interpreted], and if somebody considers that to be the Greater Serbia, it's a different issue. However, if somebody starts to fragment the state, then it is only logical to take away what they brought into the state in the first place.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a second. And this objective that you are talking about in order - how could I say this? - to reclaim its 1918 borders, I was wondering whether this objective was going to be reached through peaceful means or through military means.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: I was not one to have a say in deciding on that objective.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Were you aware of this objective, that it was to be achieved through armed force and what has been termed ethnic cleansing?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, the objective was to preserve Yugoslavia, and politicians decided on the rest.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I now voice my objection? I waited intentionally. I have the right to object to your questions, Ms. Lattanzi. I'm sure you're aware of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not convinced that you have a right to do so, but please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I waited on purpose for the witness to finish his answer in order not to influence his answer. I protest, Ms. Lattanzi, to your words, that the ideology of the Greater Serbia developed in the sense that Serbia became the Greater Serbia and included occupied territories in Bosnia which where Serbs were a majority. Who was it who occupied those territories? Was it the Serbs who did it to themselves? You are accepting the ideology of a certain [indiscernible]. How could the Serbs occupy themselves? I protest against such an interpretation on your part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I asked for clarification from the witness. Sir, I would like to know this now: I would like to know something about the relations between the accused and Milosevic, President Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question is an important one, and our break is also important. We shall have a 20-minute break now. After that, we shall resume around 10 minutes to 6.00. And if my colleague finishes in the time that has been allotted, Ms. Biersay can start on her cross-examination or, rather, questions put by the Prosecution, because we are dealing with a witness of the Court. A 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The court is back in session. Judge Lattanzi.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to raise a short procedural issue, if I may. Your Honours, you assigned two hours to the Trial Chamber, two hours to the OTP, and two hours to the Defence, and the question that I would like to ask is whether the Trial Chamber has the right to go on for longer than two hours. Your two hours have expired, if we deduct from that time my objections, the Prosecutor's objections, and the procedural issues. Maybe you have the right to surpass the time, but I would like to know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will answer straight away. I don't believe we've had two hours. I have spent a lot of time reading out oral decisions, and I haven't put many questions. Judge Harhoff perhaps exceeded the 40 minutes, I don't know, and my colleague has just started. So in the overall time, I'm not so sure. Second question. This is a witness of the Court, and the Judges take the time they feel is necessary. We have decided to grant the Prosecution two hours and to grant you two hours. If we had decided to question this witness for 10 days, we would be entitled to do so and say the Prosecutor will have one hour and the Defence one hour. This is a matter of discretion for the Bench. We said the Trial Chamber would have two hours, the Prosecution two hours, and the Defence two hours. That said, the questions must relate to the important issues which people are familiar with now; the sending of volunteers, the potential co-operation between Seselj and Milosevic. So I believe that Judge Lattanzi will have finished in half an hour's time, maybe, and Ms. Biersay can then start, which means that the Prosecutor can use its two hours and you can use your two hours. Normally speaking, this should be our last witness, so the questions are very specific and go to the heart of this case. This is what I wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope this is not the last witness. I hope that there will be another two witnesses. We shall see. If you know anything about this, because if you don't know anything about it, do not reply. Do you know what the relations were between Mr. Seselj and Milosevic, President Milosevic, before the war and during the war?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, Mr. Seselj and Mr. Milosevic were political opponents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was also the case during the entire time of the war?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Well, I learned from the media in 1997 that they were together in the government of national salvation, if my memory serves me right. That was after the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question I put to you related to the war. I asked you the question "during the war."

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... political opponents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If they were political opponents, did it make sense to ask for assistance from the JNA - how did you respond to Judge Harhoff - to ask for volunteers from the SRS as well? Perhaps it does make sense if you explain it to us.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: I assume that they had common interests, and that was to preserve Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What were the relations between Mr. Seselj and Arkan?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, their relations were never good. Just the opposite was true; they were enemies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we set aside their personal relations, I would like to talk about their public relations, i.e., sharing a common objective. The volunteers of the SRS were co-operating with the volunteers?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: We never co-operated. I don't understand the meaning of the word "co-operate." We never co-operated with the volunteers of the Serb volunteer guards or Arkan's volunteers, but they were there in the region. But we never allowed ourselves to enter an armed conflict with them, because we were on the same side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe I didn't quite understand what you said earlier. But at some point, from what I understood, you said that all these volunteers were placed under the command of Arkan's men in a particular area. But maybe I misunderstood you.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: You misunderstood something. I never said that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I must have confused this with something else. I'm sorry. They, therefore, never took part in joint operations?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Within the Territorial Defence, we had our tasks, our unit had its tasks, and I suppose that they also had their tasks and assignments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So there were no joint assignments. Assignments were always given by the TO to the men?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: While I was deputy chief of the War Staff, there were no joint missions. How shall I put it? The Territorial Defence decided on who would be sent on what mission, but we made sure never to be in the same sector. They were sometimes 20 kilometres away from us, but that had nothing to do with any sort of co-operation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. According to what you have said, incidents took place that had been provoked by volunteers of the SRS or, rather, Chetnik volunteers. You mentioned, for instance, something which occurred in 1992 at Loznica, the Loznica volunteers who were sent off to Zvornik. The head of this group was Zuca. He was a member of the Serbian Radical Party, was he?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: I can't speak about the period after 1992 because I was no longer deputy chief of the War Staff, and everything that I could share with you is hearsay. And as far as Vojin Vuckovic goes, also known as Zuca, he was our volunteer in 1991, but I heard that later on he was excluded from the membership.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: I don't know when.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues]... excluded from the party.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... are volunteering in East Slavonia in the events that took place in 1991. If we're talking about 1991, he was there.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "You don't know on what date he was excluded from the party?" Previous question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you remember a visit made by Mr. Seselj in Zvornik in the spring of 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: In spring 1992?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, I didn't hear your answer.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Well, I asked you whether you wanted to know about spring 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj was not in Zvornik in spring 1992. He was there in 1990, but that was before the conflicts broke out in Bosnia and Herzegovina, if my memory serves me well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You made a mistake when you mentioned this visit in two of your statements?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: What I said or what is perhaps written in that statement, that was the suggestion of the OTP if it says that he was there in spring 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to know this: When the Chetnik volunteers talked about the Ustashas, what did they mean by that? Did they include all the Croats, did they include some Croats, did they include the men that could go to war, the able-bodied men? What did they mean when they used this term?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Only those who waged the war, who bore arms. Military-age, able-bodied men carrying weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The volunteers that were in Vukovar, what was their aim? Was their aim for all these combatants or fighters to be killed; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: The objective of the Serbian volunteers in Vukovar was to free Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In two of your statements, you mention something which had purportedly been said by Mr. Seselj, Not a single Ustasha should leave Vukovar alive. Is this a mistake that you have made in your statement? Is this something which the Prosecutor has suggested to you? What is this?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: I don't think that was recorded authentically. He didn't say that, or at least I don't remember that Mr. Seselj said that. We appealed to them several times to surrender, and I was in Vukovar, too. And, of course, if somebody doesn't surrender, everyone knows what happens next.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But you said that this was said in the presence of 50 people, all these details?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: I did not say that in that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have another question. What about the volunteers? Well, there were those volunteers that had been -- or got themselves organised in Belgrade. Some had got themselves organised locally and some had come from Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But these were still volunteers, if we talk about Chetnik volunteers? These were still volunteers who were working together with the same objective in mind, whether these were local volunteers or whether these were volunteers coming from Belgrade; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Of course. All Serbs naturally had the same aim, and I'm talking now about patriots.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These Chetnik volunteers, when they were organised, when they were recruited, well, were speeches being addressed to them?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What were they being told?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: That they had to go fight courageously, honorably, in the spirit of the Serbian Army. They had to obey the prevailing rules, the Geneva Conventions, and the Rules and Customs of War.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Who held these speeches? Was it Mr. Seselj or was there someone else who addressed himself to these volunteers before they left?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Once or twice, Mr. Seselj said that. Once or twice, Mr. Ljubisa Petkovic and I, myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You talked to them about the Geneva Conventions, that one must abide by the Geneva Conventions? That is what you deny in your statements.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: As I said, I don't know what's in that statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You did not sign these statements?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: I did sign them, but I never got them to read or to correct if something is not consistent with the truth, although I had insisted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And why did you sign these statements? Did someone actually hold your hand so that you signed these? Did someone force you to sign these?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: I said in my introductory remarks how my statement was taken. I suppose you can understand from all that why I signed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm awfully sorry, but I have not understood at all. One last point -- last question I wanted to put to you. Incidents occurred when there is a war, and this is something which you mention in your statements. There are always incidents where volunteers were involved in something which did not meet the Geneva Convention requirements. This is something you mentioned yourself in your statements, and I would like to know this: Were there any reactions to this on the part of an organisation, a group or -- that had drafted these men? You said that these people had been chosen, and you made sure that you were not drafting, in these groups, alcoholics and the like. Did someone do anything? How did this organisation that had recruited them and chosen them react to this?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: I have to explain a couple of things to the honourable Trial Chamber. In the field, it was the Territorial Defence Staff that had operative command over the volunteers or the military unit acting in that area. We had no operative command in the field whatsoever. If something happened involving volunteers, but not only volunteers of the SRS, the locals as well, then the local military command was in charge and they had to react. There was also the civilian police on the ground. The Serbian Radical Party had no operative command whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is something I understand perfectly well. I was not actually referring to that. I was referring to the moral authority of this organisation that had screened these men and that were involved due to their behaviour, so it was for them to react. I'm not talking about only reaction in the form of a criminal sanction. I was asking you whether this organisation was checking that the volunteers were behaving properly on the battle-field.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: The only responsibility, the only competence we had, was to expel such a person from the party.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So this was always done after having been informed about something that had happened, i.e., one or other volunteer misbehaving?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: While I was part of the staff of the Serbian Radical Party, I regularly did that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In your statements, you say something else. Thank you very much. I have finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I have a follow-up question for you, which is going to be an extremely short question. Please listen carefully. I'm putting this question to you because you answered the questions put by my colleagues in a very clear way. I have the feeling that you are an educated man and you have some knowledge of political matters, because in the 1990s you were affiliated to a political movement. And I feel that you are perhaps the last witness, and therefore I feel it necessary to put this question to you. In the indictment, the Prosecutor alleges that there was a form of ethnic cleansing in Vojvodina. As you know, Vojvodina is a province which is specific and distinct from Serbia, but it is part of the Republic of Serbia. Mr. Seselj gave an interview to a press agency called "Tanjug," and this is to be found in the Prosecution Exhibit 1732. And a question is put to him about Kosovo. Mr. Seselj has already discussed Kosovo at length with us, and he says, and I have the text before me - this is on page 12 in the English version. It states that Kosovo Metohija [realtime transcript read in error "Medjugorje"], an integral part of Serbia, and of the Yugoslav republic, because at the time he gives his interview the Yugoslav republic still exists, and he says as follows. He says that on the 6th of April, 1941, there was 360.000 Albanians emigrated to Kosovo, and that as far as he was concerned, since Albania is a democratic country, there is no reason why these refugees should remain in Kosovo. One could, therefore, infer that according to him, he felt that these Albanian people in Kosovo should go back to Albania. This is what he says in his interview, which is Exhibit 1732. Based on that, and if I take a closer look at the history of your country, I have realised there have been several waves of immigration. In 1690 - perhaps you know, perhaps you don't know - there was a great wave of immigration. At the time, there was a conflict between Austria and the Turks, and as part of the coalition, strangely enough, there was the Republic of Venice which was involved and which everybody knows is Italian. There was Austria, there was Russia, and Serb farmers called Heduc [phoen], and this coalition lost against the Turks. So the patriarch then organised a wave of immigration, and Serbs were to be saved, and 40.000 to 200.000 Serbs left for Vojvodina and Slavonia, i.e., Croatia. So a great number of Serbs left for Croatia. In 1737, the war broke out with the Turks again. They were defeated, and a new wave of emigration occurred, and the Serbs left for Croatia then also. When I read this again and if I set it against the backdrop of what Mr. Seselj said about the Albanians in Kosovo, as far as you are concerned, the Serbs that had emigrated to Croatia, do you think that they should have returned to Serbia, since Serbia is a democratic country, in 1991, 1992, 1993? Seemingly, maybe not, but it was a state, in the same way that the Albanians could return to Albania. What do you think about what Mr. Seselj was saying about Kosovo, and could his theory not be applied to the Serbs that had left for Croatia?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have an objection, Mr. President. In line 18, we have on the transcript "Kosovo Medjugorje" instead of "Kosovo Metohija." This is not an accident that I'm intervening against the interpretation. There are too many Croats among our interpreters. How did "Medjugorje" find itself here along with "Kosovo"? Medjugorje is the false place of worship where they imagine our lady appeared to them. Medjugorje and Kosovo had nothing to do with each other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We shall not discuss the Virgin Mary that appeared in Medjugorje. I believe that the Pope is going to Fatima in Portugal today.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is being done by interpreters, not me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is, of course, Kosovo Metohija and not Medjugorje. That makes sense, of course. So I didn't follow the transcript. When I put a question, I look at the witness, and I do not always have my nose on the transcript like Anglo-Saxon Judges do. I would rather look at the witness, or the Prosecutor, or the accused. So can you answer my question, Witness?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I am not an expert in history. Mr. Seselj is an incomparably greater expert in the area. Therefore, I'm reluctant to discuss the subject. But as far as Vojvodina is concerned, I know about that because I've read a lot in the press, seen a lot on television. Mr. Seselj did not say that Croats need to move out of Vojvodina. Instead, he recommended that they swap properties with Serbs in Croatia. That's what I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you can answer questions about Vojvodina and not about other issues. Thank you very much. Ms. Biersay, you have 25 valuable minutes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, while I rearrange my position here, I would like to hand this binder of the B/C/S versions of the witness's various statements, and I'll give that over. And in the interim, could I please have Exhibit P27 called up while I rearrange.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, P27, please. Ms. Biersay, is that the document that is on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Go to the B/C/S page 1, around paragraph 11, and the English, I believe, would be page 2. I will get to it, but I wanted to have it ready to go.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Good evening, Mr. Rankic. My name is Lisa Biersay. I -- as you may well have guessed, I am with the Office of the Prosecutor, and I'm going to be asking you questions on behalf of the Prosecution today. Now, I'm introducing myself because we have never met before; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now, I had handed to you a binder of some statements that you have signed. And before we get to those, I see that you have some other documents on your table. Could you tell us what those documents in the pink and blue folders are?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Those documents were my responses to subpoenas and more subpoenas, an aide-memoire for me, and so on. But I'm not using it here, as you can see. But if the Court wants a document from me, I have to have it on me to be able to produce it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Could I ask you, please, to turn to tab 3 in your binder before you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am nonplussed for the first time since this trial began. What is this aide-memoire all about? I don't know anything about an aide-memoire of the witness. Who gave him an aide-memoire?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a second. We don't seem to have any translation into French. Very well. Mr. Seselj, what did you want to say?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Biersay asked the witness about some sort of aide-memoire. This is the first time I'm hearing about an aide-memoire. Where did it come from? Who gave him that aide-memoire, or did the witness himself prepare it? This is the first time I hear of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Hopefully this will not be [overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is no aide-memoire. I'm just repeating -- I'm going to repeat. The witness said that he had a folder with all the subpoenas and the answers, as well as personal files that could help jog up his memory, but he's not using it, he's not entitled to use it, and he will only answer to the questions based on the documents that have been put forward by Ms. Biersay. So, Ms. Biersay, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'd understood Ms. Biersay was asking him about the file that she had just given him. I don't see any other file. Maybe somebody placed this lectern right between me and the witness, so I can't see what he has before him. I just saw the file given him by Ms. Biersay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Biersay, you gave the witness a binder. I was wondering why Mr. Seselj does not have the same binder, because that would help us to gain some time.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, as well as the Trial Chamber, has these statements of the witness. What has been given to the witness are simply the B/C/S versions of what was contained in the very first compliance binder 1 given to the Court and given to the accused. So hopefully I can proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'd like you to turn to paragraph 14 of that statement. And the one specifically that we're looking at now is the one that is dated September 19th, 2006. Judge Lattanzi asked you some questions about what it meant to be fighting on the behalf of the Serbian cause, and you made a distinction between that struggle, what it was in 1990 versus what it was in 1991. Do you remember those questions asked by Judge Lattanzi, Mr. Rankic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: I remember the question, but I don't see it in paragraph 14. Something different is written there.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Exactly. Now, you described to Judge Lattanzi that the purpose -- the Serb cause, as you saw it, in 1990, was to preserve Serb tradition and Serb culture and Serb script. Do you remember saying that to her at page 63 of the transcript?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. The witness was saying that about the SAVA organisation, not the Serbian Chetnik Movement, and that was in response to Judge Lattanzi's question about the SAVA organisation.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Do you recall making a distinction between the purpose of the Serb cause in 1990 and 1991, yes or no, or would you like me to have it read back to you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: You remember?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And you described the purpose as being to preserve the Serbian tradition and culture and script. That's what you told the Trial Chamber; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now, I'd now like to turn your attention to the paragraph 14 of your September 2006 statement. And what follows in that statement is an excerpted portion of the political platform; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. You said "2006"?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: No. Just look under tab 3. Are you there? And perhaps you could be assisted. Well, while you're being assisted, could you tell the Trial Chamber where, in the political programme of the Serbian Chetnik Movement -- tab 3, page 4 of your --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So it would be paragraph 14 which commences on page 4. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And for the Court's ease, it is also -- the original document is Exhibit P27, which is what is on the screen currently.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Could you tell the Trial Chamber where, in the Serbian Chetnik programme, there is any mention of preserving Serb tradition, culture, and script? Do you recall that being in the platform, the 1990 Serbian Chetnik Movement platform?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. Your Honours, the gentleman never said that about the Serbian Chetnik Movement. Ms. Lattanzi, you will remember --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm talking to the Trial Chamber. I'm not talking to Ms. Biersay. Do you remember, Ms. Lattanzi, that the witness told you about the Serb Chetnik Movement, or was he talking about the organisation called SAVA and the Serbian Renewal Movement? You did not ask him about the programme of the Serbian Chetnik Movement. Kindly, can -- find it in the transcript, please. It is not in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I am asking him about the Serbian Chetnik Movement. I am asking him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, I believe that my colleague was putting a question of a general nature, and you had the Chetnik Serbian Movement, the SAVA association. The question was of a general nature, and so was the answer. Now, going from the general nature of the question, Ms. Biersay is going to a specific question, and she's showing you the platform of the Chetnik Movement, which is at paragraph 14. So there we go. This is how I see things. Ms. Biersay, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Was the focus of the Serbian Chetnik Movement -- was it focused on the tradition, the culture, and the script of the Serbian people?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: I would have to answer to the Trial Chamber and to you, of course, what I said a minute ago, I meant the year 1990 and the SAVA and the Renewal Movement, and the Serbian Chetnik Movement had its own programme which is --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about the SAVA. I am asking you about the Serbian Chetnik Movement. My question to you is: Where, in the platform of the Serbian Chetnik Movement, published in 1990, where does it say that the purpose of the movement is to protect Serb culture, script, and tradition? Maybe the answer is it doesn't, and maybe the answer is it does. I would like to know which way your answer is.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: That does not exist here, it's not written in here.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Well, it's not written in there, being your statement. Is there -- before you is Exhibit P27, which is the platform. Does it exist in the platform that's on your screen, as far as you recall? Let me ask you another question. If you -- again in paragraph 14, Roman numeral IV, in the platform it specifically discusses and says: " ... raising of the question of the responsibility for genocide committed and wartime destruction." Do you see that? " ... by those persons whose members --"

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: I see that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: "-- took part en masse in the attempt to exterminate the Serbs during the Second World War." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So in 1990, before the events, certainly, of 1991 and 1992, the Serbian Chetnik Movement's political programme discussed the issue of genocide against the Serbs during the Second World War; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Yes, but that was always part of the agenda. That question was always something that needed to be resolved and answered.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And in that very paragraph, it continues that: "The independent state of Croatia, the appearance of a new Ustasha leader ..." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So it reads: "Particularly so in the circumstances of the restoration of the independent state of Croatia and the appearance of a new Ustasha leader, as well as the general protection of the Serb population which is presently endangered by the new genocidal policy." That's what's written there; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And that is what is written in the programme, the political programme of the Serbian Chetnik Movement; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Well, probably, if this is well presented.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So in 1990, the association with the state of Croatia with the new Ustasha leader was already being put forth by the Serbian Chetnik Movement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: That was a fear from a new genocide.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And so the Serbian Chetnik Movement's political programme was based on the idea of addressing past wrongs that had been committed against the Serbian people?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: No, but rather that the Serbian people had to be reminded of what had happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Be reminded, yes. And on that point, in his speeches Mr. Seselj almost always reminded people about the past wrongs committed against the Serbs in World War II, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Well, that was part of the programme. I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: That was part of the programme. And part of the programme, as we see here again in the same paragraph, is the idea of expulsion of Albanian emigrants and their offspring. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now, Judge Lattanzi asked you some questions, I believe, about this concept of Greater Serbia, and you responded that you didn't use those terms or that term; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: No. I believe that the Great Serbia does not exist. We're talking about a territory that Serbia brought into the territory of Yugoslavia in the first place. And if somebody thinks then that that is Greater Serbia [as interpreted], then that's a different story.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Well, let's talk about that different story. I am not talking now about the concept -- let's leave the concept of Greater Serbia aside for a minute. I'm more interested at this time in the --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, again the interpretation was not good. The witness's answer was misinterpreted: [In English] " ... and if somebody thinks that that is Greater Serbia, then that's a different story." [Interpretation] And what about what he actually said, that that's for him normal Serbia? I'm very well inclined today to follow the interpretation. I've not done it before, or I did it only rarely, but what the witness did -- actually said has not been interpreted. He said that that's a normal Serbia for him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed, in the French version I heard "normal Serbia." So, Witness --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But it's not in the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed. So, Witness, what was the exact words that you used in your answer? And I'm asking the interpreters to interpret the witness very close to his words.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said the following: In a divorce case, everybody takes out what they had brought in, and for me it's normal Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the publication -- the magazine -- the newspaper called "Velika Srbija"?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And was "Velika Srbija" a newspaper at the beginning of the Serbian Chetnik Movement, when it began in 1990?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And when the Serbian Chetnik Movement evolved with the SRS, "Velika Srbija" then became the newspaper for the SRS; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: In the discourses of the accused that you heard or attended, would he use the phrase "Greater Serbia"?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, yes. But Mr. Seselj is not ashamed of that. He still uses the term.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'm not asking you to opine about shame or no shame. I am simply asking you whether or not you've ever heard him use that phrase in his many discourses.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A follow-up question to you, Witness. Unfortunately, I cannot follow the political activity in your country in Serbia, but I was wondering whether today some political figures talk about Greater Serbia, or is this what -- all those words, are they no longer used?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know, currently nobody in Serbia talks about that. We are a state under occupation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You say that you're a state under occupation. Occupied by whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] NATO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Biersay, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'm asking you these questions because on page 64 of the transcript, you said -- in response to the question posed by the Trial Chamber, you said: "I don't use that term 'Greater Serbia' at all." Do you remember that? Do you remember telling the Trial Chamber that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: But although you now say that you don't use the phrase "Greater Serbia" at all, it was a core part of the language used by the accused in his discourses; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj knows why he did that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'm not, again --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: And for me, it's nothing but normal Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'm not asking you to go into his [overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, Ms. Biersay insists on notorious matters that I never denied during these proceedings, and she's trying to portray the witness as an expert who is now -- you're not receiving interpretation. I never contested having used the term. These are notorious facts, and now she puts him in the position of an expert who is here to interpret my words and what I meant when I used them. That's ridiculous.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think that Ms. Biersay is venturing into this area, because I would have cut her off. She's trying, through her questions, to bring to light something that I'm waiting for, so let's wait and see.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: In paragraph 15 of the statement that's before you, you describe that the Greater Serbia was the concept that was set out in the first goal of the platform of the Serbian Chetnik Movement; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I would first have to look at the concept.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Well, look at it: "... the restoration of a free, independent, and democratic Serbian state that would include the whole of Serbdom and all Serb lands." So in your statement --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't see the term "Greater Serbia" anywhere here.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Do you see it in paragraph 15 of your statement?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: In para 15, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So you have used that phrase before in your statements?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: I may have quoted Mr. Seselj. This is not my turn of a phrase. This is not what I would normally use.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Do I have time for one more question, Your Honours? I'd like --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there are no objections, you have another two minutes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: You told the Trial Chamber that you heard the accused talk about the Geneva Conventions to SRS volunteers. You told the Trial Chamber that; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'd like you to turn to paragraph 35 of that statement, and I'd like you to look at the last two sentences in paragraph 35: "I have never heard Seselj talk of the Geneva Conventions to the SRS volunteers or during any public address. As far as I can remember, no one from the War Staff ever gave any instructions regarding the treatment of POWs."

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: These are not my words.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So this is a lie?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: No, this is not true.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And you're looking at the version of the statement in your language; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: This is a statement, but not mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: You signed that statement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Witness, just a few instructions. You will be back here at quarter past 2.00, because we have an afternoon session and my colleague Judge Harhoff has another hearing in the morning, so we will meet again in the afternoon. Until then, please have no contact with anyone, except for close members of your family. Please do not talk to journalists or anybody else, in order to avoid for anyone to say that someone has called you or threatened you in the meantime. So please don't answer the phone, unless you have phone calls from your family. You can watch television, you can read, but do not have any contact with anyone, so that when you come back at quarter past 2.00 tomorrow, it is as if we had a longer break than the ones we've had. And during the breaks, as you know, you don't have any contact with anyone. Have you understood correctly what I've just said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I wish you a good evening, as well as to everybody else, and we'll meet again tomorrow afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: 7.02 p.m., to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 12th day of May, 2010, at 2.15 p.m. 24 25
